chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Shadow Wilson, the hard-swinging drummer
summary: Wilson's concentrated, driving drumming makes everyone in the band play better.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I experienced playing with Shadow Wilson, which I felt like was one of the greatest drummers I'd ever played with.

As I said before every now and then, you play with a musician that just has something that touches you, and Shadow Wilson was one of those people who was just an excellent player. You couldn't play in a band with Shadow Wilson and be sluggish or lag behind, because he had a way, if you were what he called "shuckin'", he'd hit the drums and tell you to come on! You're lagging! And he was a very hard-swinging drummer, you know. When he started playing a piece from one, the very

beginning, the upper-left-hand-corner to the lower-right-hand-corner, he was purely concentrating on what he was doing. And which any musician like that, particularly a drummer, gives a band a spark, then it becomes contagious. It makes guys play, you know!
